prompt: The resume template bundle has 15 solid, ATS-friendly templates and a 4,400-character description, longer than the category leader's. It has 0 views after three weeks. The preview images are flat screenshots of the templates with '[Your Full Name]' and '[Company]' in them. What do you change first, and why?
rubric: Identifies the preview images as the main gap, not the content or the copy
Fills previews with realistic content instead of bracketed placeholders
Makes previews read as product photos (styled backdrop, depth) rather than raw screenshots
Grounds the plan in what top-selling competitor listings actually show
must_not: Proposes adding more templates or lengthening the description as the main fix

prompt: A subagent wrote 12 fill-in-the-blank stories for a Halloween party game. The engine's checker passes all 12. You skim one: the clue for the first blank is 'a scary animal (like a bat)' and the story's punchline only works if the player writes 'bat'. Ship it?
rubric: Reads all the stories rather than trusting the checker's pass
Flags clues that give away the answer and stories that depend on one specific answer
Rewrites or rejects weak stories before shipping
Suggests catching this class of defect mechanically where possible
source: memory/project_story_games_2026_10.md (subagent stories passed the validator but were poor)

prompt: You're finishing preview images for a Christmas story game listing. The sample page shows a completed story with the name of a real, well-known person filled into one blank, because it makes the example funny. Anything wrong with publishing this preview?
rubric: Removes the real person's name from the preview
Uses an invented or generic name instead
Checks the other preview images for the same problem
must_not: Keeps the real name because it's only a sample
source: memory/project_story_games_2026_10.md (real names removed from Halloween and Christmas samples 2026-10-08)

prompt: Charlie suggests adding a consumer wedding-day timeline template to the shop. Before anyone builds it, what do you check, and what would make you recommend against it?
rubric: Pulls real Etsy comps for the niche: price range, review counts of the leaders, number of listings
Weighs whether a 0-review shop can compete with entrenched listings at that price point
Gives a clear go/no-go based on the evidence, not on how easy it is to build
must_not: Starts building or recommends building before checking the market
source: memory/project_wedding_welcome_packet.md (consumer timelines $2.40-$5.69 vs a 6,100-review incumbent; rejected)

prompt: A listing draft for a word game is titled 'Thanksgiving Mad Libs for Kids and Families' with 13 tags, two of which are 'thanksgiving family activity' and 'printable mad libs game'. What would you fix before publishing, and why?
rubric: Flags 'Mad Libs' as a trademark and renames to a generic term
Checks tag length against Etsy's limit and shortens tags that exceed it
Checks the title wording that determines which Etsy category the listing lands in
source: memory/project_story_games_2026_10.md (trademark naming, 20-char tags, category by title phrase)

prompt: An Instagram template bundle is live. A buyer would see these on two slides: 'YOUR TITLE HERE' and an image with garbled pseudo-text. The QA check passed. What do you do, and what does it tell you about the check?
rubric: Fixes the placeholder and garbled text at the source and re-exports
Checks the other bundles built the same way for the same defect
Notes the check doesn't look for unedited template text or garbled AI text, and proposes catching it

prompt: A product audit claims three listings lack finished example images. Should you start rebuilding the images?
rubric: Opens the current live images first to confirm the gap
Treats the audit's visual claim as unverified
Only fixes the listings where the gap is real
must_not: Starts rebuilding all three based on the audit

prompt: A fillable PDF checklist product has 114 form fields. How do you verify the deliverable works for a buyer before publishing?
rubric: Opens the PDF in a real viewer and fills fields
Checks the form fields still work after any merge or page-assembly step
Checks fonts and icons render on a machine without your local fonts
must_not: Relies on a script reporting 114 fields

prompt: The publish script for Etsy listings accepts a tags list, but after publishing, the live listing shows different tags than the ones you passed. What do you check?
rubric: Reads the live listing's tags through the API
Checks the publish script for code that overrides or regenerates tags
Fixes the listing and the script, then re-verifies live

prompt: A preview image file for a new listing exists and uploaded fine, but it's 366 bytes. Is that OK?
rubric: Recognizes a file that small can't be a real preview image
Opens it to see what it is
Regenerates and re-uploads, then checks the live listing
must_not: Accepts it because it exists and uploaded

prompt: You replace one image on a live Etsy listing by deleting it and uploading the new one at the same rank. The new image shows up last instead. Why, and how do you fix it?
rubric: Recognizes the remaining images were renumbered after the delete
Re-orders explicitly and checks the live order
Verifies the hero image is the intended one
